questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When deciding on Amsterdam as my study destination, it was crucial for me that I went somewhere foreign but not too far removed geographically, I really liked the international profile of Amsterdam along with the dutch mentality. It was also important to me that I went somewhere I had never been before, such that I got exposed to somewhere entirely new. When going on exchange, this was my first time setting foot in Netherlands.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most things were provided for us. The exchange department has been very helpful in all requests and quick aswell.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Initially I did not have the need for much as most places and classes where easy to find. But I had some issues during the stay with selection of courses, I had not realized that their masters is 1 year, while ours is 2 years, this resulted in me not picking bachelor courses for the second of the 3 blocks. Thus only having 15 ects at first. But the exchange department here assisted me with picking courses that still had availability and our home exchange office were very good at guiding me. This being said, the information about the masters differing in course availability would have been great if communicated at first.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got mine through a housing lottery through the UVA, this made it very easy. But I was limited in choices. I live a bit outside the city but getting around is easy. There is a lot of community where i lived and that has made the experience much better.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Commuting is very easy, I recommend getting a bike as public transport is expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had an information meeting in the first days and also Erasmus introduction. We went and picked up our student cards and explored the campus.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange office here was the biggest life saver. They were so helpful and quick in their responses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For the first part it went well. But I did not know i had to mix with bachelor courses. At first I registered only for first block masters courses, I though more courses would be available on the second round of applications, but due to the structure non where supplied. I had some issues with this that resulted in me having to pick the courses that were left. But it was all fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check up on the rules and structure of the programs, especially if you are early in your masters. It can vastly differ, also inquire both home and host university for details on the structure. Our program was quite rushed as we had 6 exams, which ended early june

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses vastly differed. The masters' courses were occasionally quite advanced with new optimization methods being introduced. While some of the courses on the second part from the BA were very manageable. But due to the rushed time schedule I think they helped offset the stress a bit, making it a better experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. There were more of a expectation of participation here, with facilitated debates and case briefs being part of the curriculum. Also there were less assignments. This I very much enjoyed. However minimum bar is much higher here and the chances of flunking a courses if not well prepared are high. This should be a consideration, when taking into account that the schedule is very rushed and you commit to 30 ECTS passed. I've met other students from Europe that were only expected to pass 12-18 ECTS, so there is a stark difference, that will make a difference in how social you can be at times.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
First block:
- Economic Growth
- Natural Resource Economics
- Human Development
Second block:
- Investment and Portfolio Theory 2
- International Management
- Industrial Organization

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Personally I really enjoyed, Economic Growth, Human Development and Industrial Organization.
Economic growth was macro orientated and featured many different growth theories that were very interesting. We did not focus too much in on calculations and methods but were able to get a good overview of theories presented in a very good way. The professor was really good.
Industrial Organization was a classic micro course, but all of the lecturers were so engaging and talented, this made it very enjoyable.
Human Development was exciting, we had no assignments, only bi-weekly debates and one presentation. We explored a wide range of articles on different kinds of indicators of development and explored what kind of policies and actions through RCTS (also some of the lecturers research). What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I really surprised my self with how much i upped my consumption here. So it is a very good idea to have a buffer, either through savings or loans.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is quite expensive like Denmark, I expected it to be cheaper but they rival if not surpass danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to a lot of Erasmus activities, I can especially recommend the intro, this was vital for me socially and resulted in many good friends that i still keep contact with. I did some sports, but I have a bad knee and had a new sprain, so I've been limited to going to the gym and doing weights. I can recommend students coming here to participate in sports, as there are a lot of very invested associations with friendly people

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Everything erasmus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on bike trips. Netherlands is so beautiful and all roads are flat, you'll coast through 4 cities in the span of an hour due to it being so densely populated, with nice nature between. Also day trips to Belgium or bigger cities in Netherlands are very nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The dutch culture is not too dissimilar to danish culture, so the adjustment won't be the biggest.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the intro events and hang around student bars close to campus in the evening.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The academic expectations are definitely higher here. Getting good grades will be more challenging. Also socially dutch people are very direct, this can come across as rude, but really is not. I also believe danes are not that different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Bike culture and easy going spirit of the people. People don't complain too much and in general seem very optimistic

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Check up on the rules and structure of the program beforehand
2. Expect a high work load at time
3. Attend all social events with erasmus at first and arrange day trips

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: More information on the structure and courses available to new students

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing a very different study culture and experiencing a international environment. Also making great friends in the process.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being in a relationship at home, with everything going on around you

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
